conviction_note: Two readings, deliberately not fitted together. The findings sum to +1.5 because most of what I found is small, sourced, company-level support: implied Q4 EPS from the guide sits at or above every consensus quoted, there is a large buyback on a fast-shrinking Class A count, and about 16% of Class A is short with roughly 10 days to cover. The scaled number is only +0.63, because the line this stock trades on is the first FY27 guide tonight. Management has cut the outlook on three straight prints (Nov-25 -10.5%, May-26 -7.7%, Aug-26 -20.5%), and the stock is already up about 36% off its 30 Sep low with shorts covering, so p_up moves only to 53. abs_move stays at the 9.9% historical median plus a little for a first FY27 guide and a crowded short.
bar: Q4 FY26 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026) revenue $54.5M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IIIV/earnings-forecasts) and $55.5M (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/IIIV/estimates). The two sources roughly agree, and both sit inside the company's implied Q4 guide of $52.7-57.7M (FY $216-221M less 9M $163.3M, per the Q3 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1728688/000172868826000041/i3verticalsq3fy2026earning.htm). The EPS bar is DISPUTED: $0.24 (Benzinga), $0.27 (Chartmill), $0.19 (Earnings Whispers), against an implied guide of $0.26-0.30 (FY $1.08-1.12 less 9M $0.82). The EPS-dependent finding is therefore capped small. The real bar is the FY27 guide: in Aug-26 management pre-framed mid-single-digit revenue growth (down from high-single) with 100-200bp adj. EBITDA margin expansion, which implies roughly $227-232M revenue on a ~$218.5M FY26 base. I found no sourced FY27 consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest is 2,851,058 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, 295k ADV, 9.66 days to cover (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/iiiv/shortinterest). That is about 15.8% of the 18.02M Class A shares outstanding on 6 Aug 2026, and more of the true float, since Class B is 8.3M held by insiders. Shorts are covering: 3.49M at 15 Sep, 3.32M at 30 Sep, 2.96M at 15 Oct, 2.85M at 30 Oct. No option chain exists (empty_chain), so there is no skew. Run-up: 20d +10.4%, 5d -2.5%, 35% below the 52-week high, about 36% above the 52-week low (low $13.82 on 30 Sep). New long holders filed 13Gs: T. Rowe Price Investment Management 9.3% (event 30 Sep), Vanguard Capital Management 5.01% (30 Sep), Forager 6.1% (1 Sep). Crowded short with active covering, so any negative is shrunk.

findings.finding: The company has been shrinking the share count hard with borrowed money. Class A shares fell from 23.98M (30 Sep 2025) to 18.24M (30 Jun 2026) and 18.02M (6 Aug 2026). In fiscal Q3 it repurchased 2,312,558 shares for $48.6M at $20.78. The $60M Feb-2026 program is exhausted, and a $100M program authorized 12 May 2026 runs to May 2027. Revolver debt went from $0 to $114.3M (1.9x leverage), and cash fell from $66.7M to $2.6M. After that, the stock traded $13.8-17 through Sep-Oct, below every price the company paid. The Q4 release should disclose Sep-quarter repurchases, a lower diluted count behind adj. EPS, and possibly a new or refreshed authorization.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback announced with the Q1 FY26 print (Feb-26 program adopted 5 Feb) coincided with +5.3%. The May-26 $100M authorization came days after a -7.7% print and did not stop the decline. The buyback has not overridden a guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The Sep-quarter repurchase volume is not public until tonight's release and 10-K. If the market had priced a large Sep-Oct buyback at $14-17, the stock would not have sat 35% below its high with 16% of Class A short. The ~36% rally off the 30 Sep low may partly be this bid, so part of it is priced.
findings.independence: Same company filings as the revolver finding (different document: 8-K 2026-10-09, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1728688/000172868826000048/iiiv-20261009.htm). The Q3 release CEO quote, '>20% of outstanding shares repurchased since Oct 2024', is the same fact (https://quartr.com/events/i3-verticals-inc-iiiv-q3-2026_ofpv5jPE).

findings.finding: Implied Q4 FY26 adj. diluted EPS from the company's own guide is $0.26-0.30 (FY $1.08-1.12 less 9M actual $0.82). Every quoted consensus sits at or below the bottom of that range: Benzinga $0.24, Chartmill $0.27, Earnings Whispers $0.19. Merely landing inside the guide would print a nominal EPS beat. Implied Q4 revenue is $52.7-57.7M (midpoint $55.2M) against a $54.5-55.5M consensus, and implied Q4 adj. EBITDA is $13.5-16.5M (FY $57-60M less 9M $43.5M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 adj. EPS of $0.25 met the $0.25 consensus while revenue missed ($53.1M vs ~$55.0M), and the stock fell 20.5% on the guide cut. This name trades on the guide, not on the EPS line.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators carry stale or mixed EPS estimates (0.19/0.24/0.27). If the market had anchored on the guide-implied $0.26-0.30, previews would quote a consensus at or above $0.26. This lands INSIDE the company's guide, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect. It is capped small because the bar is disputed.
findings.independence: Consensus figures from Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IIIV/earnings-forecasts) and Chartmill (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/IIIV/estimates). The guide arithmetic rests on the same Q3 8-K as the transportation and guidance findings.

findings.finding: On 9 Oct 2026 the company replaced its May-2023 credit agreement (commitments $400M, maturing May 2028) with a $350M amended and restated senior secured revolver with JPMorgan. Pricing is SOFR +1.50-2.50%, covenants are max 4.0x net leverage and min 3.0x interest coverage, and there is an accordion of the greater of $100M or 100% of LTM EBITDA. Leverage was 1.9x at 30 Jun. The facility is a refinancing and maturity extension that keeps buyback and M&A capacity, not a distress financing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing. The 9 Oct 8-K landed while the stock was rising off its 30 Sep low.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since 9 Oct, so mostly priced. What the money buys: the Q3 10-Q shows the prior revolver funded $138M+ of buybacks and a $60M acquisition (insurance-verification business, Jan-26). The question answered is 'capital return and M&A capacity', so the sign is positive or zero. A distress read would show up as covenant-amendment language or a higher spread, and neither is present.
findings.independence: Shares the company-filing chain with the buyback finding. The Q3 10-Q shows interest coverage of 13.5x (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001728688/000172868826000045/iiiv-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Short interest was 2.85M shares at 30 Oct 2026, about 15.8% of 18.02M Class A shares outstanding, with 9.7 days to cover on 295k ADV. Shorts have covered 18% from the 3.49M peak on 15 Sep while the stock rallied ~36% off its 30 Sep low. The buyback keeps shrinking the share base those shorts sit on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was 3.0-3.5M through the -7.7% (May) and -20.5% (Aug) prints. Shorts were paid on guide cuts. The Feb-26 +5.3% print came with SI around 3.4M, with no squeeze of note.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public data. What it adds is asymmetry: a first FY27 guide that merely confirms the pre-framed mid-single-digit growth would force 10 days of covering into a thin tape. If the market saw no squeeze risk, short interest would not be falling into the print. If it saw a big one, the 20d run-up would be larger than +10%.
findings.independence: The covering trend corroborates the price low of $13.82 on 30 Sep (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IIIV/charts). Separate filers' 13Gs show long accumulation (next finding).

findings.finding: Three long-only institutions crossed the 5% line after the August guide cut: T. Rowe Price Investment Management at 9.3% (1,672,506 Class A, event 30 Sep 2026, filed 16 Nov), Vanguard Capital Management at 5.01% (904,542, event 30 Sep, filed 30 Oct), and Forager Capital at 6.1% (1,106,474, event 1 Sep, filed 30 Sep). About 20% of Class A sits in these three alone, alongside the company's own repurchases.
findings.why_not_priced: The filings are public, so mostly priced. The T. Rowe 13G was filed only yesterday. The float available to cover a 2.85M short is smaller than the share count suggests. Holders of size, not hedge funds, would make the reaction to a disappointing guide less violent than August's -20%.

findings.finding: Peer read: Tyler Technologies, the largest US public-sector software and payments peer, reported Q3 2026 on 28 Oct, after i3 last spoke. Transaction revenues grew 9.5% (14.2% excluding the Texas wind-down), up from 3.5% in Q2. ARR grew 11%, the FY26 revenue outlook was maintained, and the SaaS bookings mix shifted toward transaction-funded motor-vehicle titling and regulatory deals. i3's proprietary payments line ($13.3M of $53.1M in Q3) and its statewide transportation/motor-vehicle insurance verification business sit in the same end-markets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: i3's Q3 payments shortfall (>$1M) came from net take rates (commercial-card interchange), not volume. A peer's volume acceleration does not fix that line.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer print came three weeks before i3's, and i3 previews do not reference it. It is a proxy only: i3's problems were utilities professional services and take rates, which Tyler's print does not touch. Sized small accordingly.
findings.independence: Proxy. Tyler summary also at https://quartr.com/events/tyler-technologies-tyl-q3-2026_3gH3zzgH (same print).

findings.finding: In the Q3 release the CEO said four statewide Transportation services went live in the quarter and should help re-accelerate recurring revenue growth. Q3 recurring revenue was $43.5M (+8%) and non-recurring $9.5M (-18%). The go-lives give Q4 a full quarter of their recurring revenue, supporting the sequential step the guide midpoint needs (Q3 $53.1M to Q4 $55.2M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Recurring growth was already 8-12% in each FY26 print. The stock fell on the last two anyway because non-recurring and the guide disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: Management already told the market, so it is inside the guided range and mostly priced. What remains unpriced is the magnitude: if Q4 recurring re-accelerates to double digits, FY27's mid-single-digit frame looks conservative. Net of the rest: non-recurring (~18% of revenue) fell 18% in Q3 and the utilities project is delayed (guidance finding), which can offset it.
findings.independence: Same Q3 8-K as the EPS-bar finding. Quartr summary of the same release: https://quartr.com/events/i3-verticals-inc-iiiv-q3-2026_ofpv5jPE.

findings.finding: Guidance risk, the line this stock trades on. FY26 guidance was cut at Q2 (revenue $221-229M, already reduced) and again at Q3 to $216-221M, with adj. EBITDA cut from $61-65M to $57-60M. FY27 revenue growth was taken from high- to mid-single digits. The cause was a large utilities project whose timeline 'has extended' (≈$4.5M of the $6.5M cut was professional services) plus take-rate pressure from commercial-card interchange. Tonight is the first formal FY27 guide, and the last three guide events moved the stock -10.5%, -7.7% and -20.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov-25 FY26 initial guide: -10.5%. Feb-26 raised outlook: +5.3%. May-26 cut: -7.7%. Aug-26 cut plus FY27 lowered: -20.5%. The guide has decided every reaction in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Management pre-framed FY27 at mid-single digits, so a guide of ~$227-232M with 100-200bp margin expansion is roughly priced. What is not priced is whether the utilities delay and take-rate pressure push the formal range below that frame (a fourth disappointment) or whether management sets it conservatively and beats. Sized only modestly negative: the crowded short and the 36% off-low rally cut both ways, and there is no sourced FY27 consensus.
findings.independence: Quartr summary of the same call: https://quartr.com/events/i3-verticals-inc-iiiv-q3-2026_ofpv5jPE. The guide-cut history is from the company's own 8-Ks. The crowded short (positioning finding) argues against sizing this larger.

findings.finding: Reported ARR fell sequentially: $183.5M at 31 Mar 2026 (Q2 release) to $174.1M at 30 Jun 2026 (Q3 release). The prior-year comparison also fell, from $164.5M to $160.8M, which points to a definitional recast or seasonality rather than churn. Year-on-year ARR growth decelerated from 11.6% to 8.3%. A further deceleration in Q4 ARR growth would undercut the 're-accelerate recurring' message.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ARR decelerated from 11.6% to 8.3% into the -20.5% August print, alongside the guide cut, so its separate effect is unclear.
findings.why_not_priced: Both numbers are public. The year-on-year deceleration is visible, but the sequential drop is unexplained in the release. If the market had read it as churn, short interest would have risen after August; it has fallen since mid-September. Small.
findings.independence: Q3 ARR is in the Q3 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1728688/000172868826000041/i3verticalsq3fy2026earning.htm). It shares the Q3 8-K with the transportation finding, but this finding argues the other way on recurring momentum.

findings.finding: The only Form 4 since August is the CFO's (Geoffrey Smith) tax withholding: code F, 1,476 shares at $14.78 on 20 Sep 2026, on an RSU vest, leaving 54,819 shares. There was no open-market insider buying at the 52-week low, and no insider selling.
findings.why_not_priced: It carries no information: code F is mechanical. It is filed so the panel can see the insider record is empty either way.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions list shows no other Form 4 from Aug 1 to Nov 17 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001728688.json).

searched_and_found_nothing: Analyst rating or target changes after 10 Aug 2026 (DA Davidson cut to $28 on 10 Aug is the last found). An AAII page claims 'one upgrade in the month before Nov 16', but I could not locate it.
Takeover, strategic review, activist or 13D: none found. EDGAR shows only 13G/13G-A filings.
Conference appearances or management commentary Sep-Nov 2026: none found.
New state-level contract awards Aug-Nov 2026: only small county renewals (Titus County TX $212k three-year extension, Sep 2026), immaterial.
FY27 consensus revenue/EPS: no reliable source.
Q3 FY26 call transcript text: marketbeat 403, statementdog empty, nasdaq 503, so I relied on summaries.

rejected_candidates.candidate: $9.9M unrealized gain on a minority equity investment in Q3 FY26 other income
rejected_candidates.detail: A Q3 item already reported. Nothing shows it recurring in the Q4 release window, and it is below operating income and excluded from adj. EPS.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Deferred revenue fell from $37.7M (30 Sep 2025) to $25.3M (30 Jun 2026)
rejected_candidates.detail: Most likely the seasonal public-sector billing cycle (annual billings around 30 Sep). With no prior-year June comparison in hand it adds nothing beyond the ARR finding, so it was merged into that one as context.

baseline_tension: No option skew exists. The evidence leans mildly positive (buyback, EPS bar below the guide, crowded short), but it runs into a +10% 20-day run-up and a 36% rally off the September low that already price some relief. Hence p_up only 53 against a +1.5 findings sum.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (disputed bar): EPS consensus sources disagree (0.19/0.24/0.27), so the guide-implied EPS finding was capped from +0.6 to +0.3.
Lesson 1/6 (inside the guide, verified fact is not a reaction): the transportation go-lives finding lands inside the guided range on a name that trades on the guide, so it was cut from +0.5 to +0.3.

Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): the guidance-risk finding went from -1.2 to -0.9. Short interest as a standalone positive went from +1.0 to +0.7, because public positioning is partly the information set (lesson 5).
Lesson 5 (proxy): Tyler peer read cut from +0.4 to +0.3. The 13G accumulation was cut from +0.3 to +0.2 as public positioning.
Lesson 4 (financing): the revolver was answered as refinancing for buybacks and M&A, with 1.9x leverage against a 4.0x covenant, and left at +0.2.
Buyback trimmed from +0.7 to +0.6 because the buyback has never overridden a guide cut in this name's history (lesson 1).
Scaled measurement unchanged: abs_move 10.5 and p_up 53 already carried these caveats.
